chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to me, saying: He told me Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, who said: Ibn Abi Ya'foor told me, saying: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me:

"Keep in mind the perishment of so-and-so (he mentioned a name of a man from the Abbasids), the rising of al-Sufyani, the killing of the pure innocent man, the sinking army, and the call." I said: "And what is the call? Is it the announcer?" He said: "Yes, and by it the Master of this Matter (al-Qa'im) will be known." Then he said: "The entire deliverance will be after the perishment of that man of the Abbasids."

key_terms.جَيْشُ الْخَسْفِ: the sinking army (a group that will be swallowed by the earth)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: the Master of this Matter (referring to Imam al-Mahdi)
key_terms.قَتْلُ النَّفْسِ: killing of the pure innocent man (Qatl al-Nafs)

ai.seo_question: What are the major signs preceding the appearance of Imam al-Mahdi according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the demise of a specific Abbasid figure as the pivotal event that ushers in the complete relief (al-Faraj) and the emergence of the Mahdi, linking it to other major eschatological signs such as the Sufyani, the sinking army, and a distinguishing divine call. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that political transitions within the Abbasid caliphate serve as direct precursors to the Mahdi's appearance, with the 'call' serving as a key identifier for his authority. The emphasis on 'complete relief' highlights the transition from partial concealment or minor signs to the full establishment of justice.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (16) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Ali bin al-Hasan from Ali bin Mahziyar from Hammad bin Eessa from al-Husayn bin Mukhtar from bin Abu Ya’foor that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said to him: “

Keep in mind the perishment of so-and-so (he mentioned a name of a man from the Abbasids), the rising of as-Sufyani, killing the pure innocent man, the sinking and the call, by which the man of this matter (al-Qa’im) will be known. The entire deliverance will be after the perishment of that man of the Abbasids.”
